Performance of India in the international sports events 
*226.     SHRI C. PERUMAL: 
SHRI DARA SINGH: 
Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether the performance of our country in the international sports events 
has not been upto the mark compared to that of other developing countries; 
11 

RAJYA SABHA [21 July, 2004] 
(b) if so, the reasons therefor; and 
(c) the remedial steps taken to rectify the situation? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI SUNIL DUTT): 
(a) to (c) The performance of Indian sportspersons since the Commonwealth 
Games, 2002 has been quite creditable in comparison to many other developing 
countries. India won a record haul of 69 medals (as against 25 in the last games) 
in the 2002 Commonwealth Games and secured the fourth position in the 
medals tally. Similarly, India secured 36 medals in the Busan Asian Games. Indian 
sportspersons have performed creditably in a number of international competitions 
including the 1 st Afro-Asian Games in Hyderabad in 2003 and the last SAF Games 
at Islamabad in 2004. 
Government of India, in addition to providing sports infrastructure, has taken 
the following measures to further  improve the perfo rmance of Indian 
sportspersons in various international competitions. 
(i) Finalization of Long Term Development Plans (LTDP) for various sports 
disciplines in consultation with the concerned National Sports 
Federations, former international sportspersons, sports scientists and 
experts. Plans are under implementation. 
(ii) Provision of equipment and scientific support to sportspersons. 
(iii) Intensive coaching of the players by Indian and foreign coaches in 
coaching camps. 
(iv) Financial assistance to concerned federations for participation of 
sportspersons in international tournaments. 
(v) Intensive training abroad to the teams. 
(vi) Assistance for purchase of equipment, scientific support and training and 
participation within the country and abroad under the 'Scheme relating to 
Talent Search and Training' and the 'National Sports Development 
Fund'. 
Floods in Assam 
*227. SHRI KARNENDU BHATTACHARJEE : Will the Minister of HOME 
AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government are aware about the latest situation of floods in Assam; 
12 

[21 July, 2004] RAJYA SABHA 
(b) whether Government propose to take some effective measures to control 
floods in Assam which is a regular feature particularly in Bank Valley; and 
(c) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS (SHRI 
S. RAGHUPATHY): (a) Yes, Sir. As on 18 .7.2004, 26 of the 27 districts were 
affected by floods. According to the reports received from the State Government, 
7994 villages with a population of 85.42 lakhs and 6.43 lakh hectares cropped area 
have been affected. 63 human lives have been lost and about 4.29 lakh houses 
damaged. 
(b) and (c) Flood Management including river erosion being a State subject, 
investigation, planning and implementation of Flood Management Schemes are 
within the purview of the State Government. The Central Government renders 
assistance, which is Technical, catalytical and promotional in nature and only in 
specified States under Centrally Sponsored Schemes. 
The Ministry of Water Resoruces, the nodal Ministry for floods 
Management and Control, has been ad vising and assisting the State 
Government in taking appropriate measures both structural and non-Structural 
for flood control in the State of Assam. The Brahmaputra Board has prepared 
master plans for Brahmaputra and Barak Basins and subsidiaries and these 
were sent to the State Government including Assam for appropriate action. 
The Brahmaputra Board has also taken up the execution of the Pagladiya Dam 
Project, which was approved by the Government of India in January 2001, at 
an estimated cost of Rs. 542.90 crore with full central funding. This will provide 
flood control benefit to an area of 40,000 hectares in Assam as a long term 
measure. Besides above, a number of Drainage Development/Anti Erosion 
Schemes have been taken up by the Board in Assam at an estimated cost of Rs. 
62.68 crore through 100% Central funding. This includes Harrang Drainage 
Development Scheme in Barak Valley at an estimated cost of Rs. 30.49 crore. 
As a long term measure Tipaimukh Multipurpose Project on river Barak which 
was investigated by Brahmaputra Board and DPR was prepared has since 
been transferred to North Eastern Electric Power Corporation 
13 

RAJYA SABHA [21 July. 2 004] 
(NEEPCO). This project which is located on Barak river will have flood control benefits in 
the Barak valley besides hydro electric power. The techno economic clearance has been 
given by CEA. 
In order to assist Assam and North Eastern States including Sikkim and North 
Bengal, the Ministry of Water Resources have formulated a Centrally Sponsored 
Scheme (CSS) for taking up critical flood control and anti erosion schemes in Brahmaputra 
and Barak valley, for an amount of Rs,. 166.68 crore in the ratio of 90% as Central 
share as grant (150.00 crore) and 10% as State share (Rs. 16.68 crore). The Planning 
Commission has approved the scheme for implementation during Tenth Five Year Plan.

abolished.
